name: AR-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with R+13 partisan lean
Incumbent Steve Womack has a large financial advantage ($2.4M on hand vs ~$6K)
Prediction markets price Democratic chances at about 4%
No polls or expert ratings signal competitive race
model.rationale: Womack is a well-funded incumbent in a district that leans Republican by 13 points, and markets give Ryerse only a small chance. With no polling or ratings suggesting competition, the race stays solidly Republican.
model.watch: A major late outside-spending intervention or unexpected scandal involving Womack would be the main way this becomes competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northwest Arkansas's third district is a solidly Republican seat, and Steve Womack is seeking another term with the advantages of incumbency. He has raised nearly $1.9 million and holds about $2.4 million on hand, while Democrat Robb Ryerse has raised roughly $120,000 with minimal cash remaining. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings track this race, and prediction markets give Ryerse only a small chance of winning. The district's Republican lean and the lopsided financial picture point to a comfortable Womack victory, with little evidence of a competitive dynamic developing.
